title: Ignite 2026: Edge for Business gets extension risk scores
summary: Microsoft announced Edge for Business updates. Generally available: extension safety, an organisation-wide extension inventory with Akamai and Spin.AI risk scores per extension and version to support allow/block decisions. In preview: extension leak control (stop selected organisation-installed extensions reading protected pages), a native Microsoft Sentinel connector for browser security events and audit logs, Entra Global Secure Access inside the Edge work profile so Windows users reach private web apps without a separate VPN client or agent, a managed agent-browsing mode where agents get their own window and Entra agent identity, and a skills recorder that turns recorded browser workflows into Copilot Cowork skills under IT control.
why: Browser extensions are one of the least-governed parts of most estates, and an inventory with risk scores is a practical way to start an allowlist. The agent-browsing and skills recorder previews mean agents will increasingly act inside the browser, so browser policy becomes agent policy.
todo: Do now: review the extension safety inventory and draft an allowlist or blocklist policy for high-risk extensions, starting with those that read all sites.
If you plan Global Secure Access Private Access, note the Edge integration as a possible agentless option for web apps — but test it only once it is in your tenant.
Wait: leak control, the Sentinel connector, GSA in Edge, agent browsing and skills recorder are preview — announced, not verified.
effective_note: Extension safety GA; other items preview — per Microsoft.
